_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
Keyboard focus reveals the record choices, and Escape returns focus to the button. The page fakes the microphone, screen capture and MediaRecorder, and window.__recordingMock counts what the page asked for (read it with eval, e.g. "window.__recordingMock.recorderStarts"): displayRequests (screen captures requested), synchronousDisplayRequests (those requested inside a click or keydown handler), microphoneRequests, audioSources, recorderStarts, recorderStops and stoppedTracks (media tracks stopped). "The recording state" is the data-state attribute of ".recording-status". "The record menu" is [data-testid="record-menu"]. Keys go to whatever has focus: do not click anything in this test. "X is focused" means X is document.activeElement. The message input is [data-testid="message-input"], the voice button [data-testid="voice-button"], the recording panel [data-testid="recording-panel"], and its stop, cancel and retry buttons [data-testid="recording-stop-button"], [data-testid="recording-cancel-button"] and [data-testid="recording-retry-button"]. When a step says an element should contain or have some text, assert that on that element, not with a page-wide wait_text. Perform the steps in order. 
1. Navigate to /new. The voice button should be visible.
2. Focus [data-testid="attach-button"] (eval its focus()). Press Tab.
3. The voice button should be focused, and the record menu visible.
4. Press Tab twice. The record menu's button "Voice & Screen" ('[data-testid="record-menu"] button[aria-label="Voice & Screen"]') should be focused.
5. Press Escape. No record menu may remain (count 0), and the voice button should be focused.
6. Press Enter. The recording panel should get data-mode "microphone".
